title: Surjectivity on spectra is stable under base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings whose induced map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is surjective. For every homomorphism of commutative rings $R\to R'$, the base-change map $R'\to R'\otimes_R S$, $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$, induces a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_R S)\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00FI (lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal), line 5822, final base-change assertion

proof.text: Reduction to fibre rings. Let $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image under $R\to R'$, a prime ideal of $R$. Put $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $T=(R'\otimes_RS)\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, the fibre rings of $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak p$ and of $R'\to R'\otimes_RS$ at $\mathfrak p'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective, $\mathfrak p$ is in its image, so $F\neq0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-in-image-iff-fibre-ring-nonzero] (direction 'only if') applied to $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak p$. By the same lemma (direction 'if') applied to $R'\to R'\otimes_RS$ and $\mathfrak p'$, it suffices to show $T\neq0$ (Steps 2-4).

source.place: Lemma Tag 00FI (lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal, line 5822), second paragraph of the proof, and Lemma Tag 00E7 (lemma-in-image, line 3500)

proof.text: The map of residue fields. The ring map $R\to R'$ sends $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ into $R'\setminus\mathfrak p'$ (as $\mathfrak p$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak p'$), so it induces a local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to R'_{\mathfrak p'}$, $r/s\mapsto r/s$, which maps $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ into $\mathfrak p'R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ and hence a homomorphism of fields $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Both composites $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and $R\to R'\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ send $r$ to the class of $r/1$, so they agree: the $R$-algebra structure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ through $R'$ is the one through $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Thus $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00FI (lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal, line 5822), second paragraph of the proof: '$\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an extension of fields'

proof.text: Identification of the fibre ring. Using the symmetry $M\otimes N\cong N\otimes M$ of tensor products of algebras, $T\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_RS)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with its $R\to S$, $B$, $A$ taken to be $R\to R'$, $S$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$) this is isomorphic as a ring to $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_RS$. By Step 2 the $R$-algebra $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is also an algebra over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ through $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] again (with its $R\to S$, $B$, $A$ taken to be $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $S$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$) gives a ring isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_RS$. With $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS\cong F$ (symmetry) we get a ring isomorphism $T\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}F$.
